title: SBA Lender Broker Referral Programs: How They Work and How to Win
summary: SBA lenders pay brokers about 1-3% for qualified referrals, disclosed on Form 159. Win by matching each deal to the best-fit lender.
body_markdown:
### Turn Borrower Relationships Into Funded SBA Deals


SBA lender broker referral programs give loan brokers, CPAs, and M&A advisors a structured way to earn from the borrower relationships they already have. The U.S. Small Business Administration reported[record FY25 SBA lending](https://www.sba.gov/article/2025/09/30/trump-sba-delivers-record-capital-small-businesses-fy25) , with 84,400 7(a) and 504 loans guaranteed for $44.8 billion. Lenders fill much of that pipeline through outside referral sources who already sit next to borrowers.


The brokers who win act as the orchestrator of each deal, matching every borrower to the lender most likely to approve and fund it. This guide explains how an SBA loan referral partner program works, how SBA rules treat broker pay, and how to pick lenders and close faster.


‍


### What Are SBA Lender Broker Referral Programs?


An SBA lender broker referral program is a formal arrangement where an SBA lender pays a broker who refers qualified small business borrowers. The lender underwrites, closes, and funds the loan, while the referral partner sources and pre-screens the deal.


The U.S. Small Business Administration spells out the role in its[SBA referral agent definition](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-13/chapter-I/part-103/section-103.1) at 13 CFR 103.1. A Referral Agent refers an applicant to a lender, or a lender to an applicant, and either side may employ and pay that agent.


The same regulation separates referral agents from Packagers, who are paid to prepare the applicant's SBA application. A Lender Service Provider performs lender functions, such as originating or servicing loans, for pay from the lender. SBA decides Lender Service Provider status on a loan-by-loan basis, so the label depends on the work performed on each deal.


In Lendflow's view, lenders recruit brokers because referred applications arrive pre-screened, without the direct marketing cost of finding each borrower. The broker sits in the middle of the market, sourcing and qualifying small business borrowers without holding capital. Lendflow's guide to[broker and lender partnerships](https://www.lendflow.com/post/business-broker-lender-partnerships-how-lendflow-makes-it-work-ao) shows how that structure works in practice.


#### SBA Loan Programs Brokers Can Refer Into


Three SBA programs cover most referral opportunities, and each fits a different borrower. The U.S. Small Business Administration's[SBA lender program resources](https://www.sba.gov/sba-lenders/) list 7(a) up to $5 million, 504 at $25,000 to $5.5 million, and Microloans to $50,000.


Program Maximum Amount Best-Fit Borrower


SBA 7(a) loan Up to $5 million Businesses that need working capital, acquisition financing, or refinancing


SBA 504 loan $25,000 to $5.5 million Businesses buying owner-occupied real estate or major equipment


SBA Microloan Maximum of $50,000 Very small businesses with modest capital needs, served through intermediaries


Some clients will not fit any SBA program, and brokers who also place term loans, lines of credit, and equipment financing can keep serving them. Review the[financing types Lendflow supports](https://www.lendflow.com/customers/financing-types) to see the non-SBA options available alongside SBA loans.


#### Preferred Lenders, Bank Lenders, and Non-Bank SBLCs


Lender status shapes how a referred deal moves through SBA review. Per SBA's lender resources, Preferred Lender Program (PLP) delegated authority lets a lender process, close, and service certain 7(a) loans without prior SBA review. Lenders without that authority process loans through SBA's Loan Guaranty Processing Center.


Under[13 CFR Part 120](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-13/chapter-I/part-120) , the U.S. Small Business Administration defines a Small Business Lending Company (SBLC) as a non-depository lending institution that is SBA-licensed. The same rules state that SBA monitors, supervises, examines, and regulates SBA Supervised Lenders, which include SBLCs. Some non-bank SBA lenders fall into other categories, so confirm a partner's license type before you refer.


Lender Type Approval Authority Oversight


PLP bank Delegated authority to approve certain 7(a) loans without prior SBA review Depository bank


Non-PLP bank Non-delegated processing through SBA's Loan Guaranty Processing Center Depository bank


Non-bank SBLC Authorized by SBA to make 7(a) loans; processing path depends on its SBA delegation status Non-depository lender licensed and supervised by SBA


Each lender also applies its own credit policy on top of SBA rules, so compare several lenders before treating a decline as final. A one-lender referral relationship can leave approvable deals on the table.


‍


### How SBA Lender Broker Referral Programs Work, Step by Step


Most programs follow the same six-step path from signed agreement to paid referral. Brokers who[submit to multiple lenders](https://www.lendflow.com/post/best-software-for-a-loan-broker-to-submit-to-multiple-lenders) through one application avoid re-sending the same file to one lender at a time.


1. Join the program by signing the lender's referral agreement, which sets compensation terms and submission standards.
2. Pre-qualify the borrower on SBA eligibility, cash flow, equity, and, for acquisitions, the buyer's industry experience.
3. Submit the referral with organized financial statements, the borrower's résumé, and details on any business being acquired.
4. The lender underwrites the file, requests missing items, and issues an approval or a decline.
5. The lender closes and funds the loan once its conditions and any third-party reports are complete.
6. The lender pays your compensation as agreed and discloses it to SBA on Form 159.


#### How Brokers Get Paid Under SBA Rules


Lendflow reports that business loan brokers typically earn 1% to 3% of the funded amount, paid by the lender. That range reflects common market practice, since SBA sets no numeric cap and instead requires fees to be disclosed and reasonable.


The U.S. Small Business Administration requires[SBA Form 159 fee disclosure](https://www.sba.gov/document/sba-form-159-fee-disclosure-compensation-agreement) , signed by lender and applicant, whenever either party pays an agent. Per the form's instructions, an agent may not be paid by both the applicant and the lender for the same service.


Agents must also sign a compensation agreement under the U.S. Small Business Administration's[SBA compensation agreement rule](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-13/chapter-I/part-103/section-103.5) at 13 CFR 103.5. If SBA deems a fee unreasonable, the agent must reduce the charge or refund the excess to the applicant.


Confirm you are using the current edition of Form 159 before each closing, because form editions change. Clean, compliance-ready disclosures also show lender partners that your deals will hold up to SBA review.


### Best Practices for Choosing Lender Partners and Closing Faster


The lender you choose affects whether a deal closes, how much the borrower receives, and how quickly funds arrive. The practices below help brokers match each file to the right partner and keep it moving.


#### Evaluate Lender Partners on Fit, Not Just Fee


The Federal Reserve Banks'[Small Business Credit Survey](https://www.fedsmallbusiness.org/-/media/project/clevelandfedtenant/fsbsite/reports/2026/2026-report-on-employer-firms/2026-report-on-employer-firms.pdf) found 42% of applicants got the full amount, 36% got some or most, and 22% got none. Applicants at small banks were more likely to be fully approved, at 57%, than applicants at other lenders. The March 2026 report draws on a convenience sample of 6,525 employer firms, yet it suggests that outcomes vary by lender type.


Score each potential partner on PLP status, credit box, programs offered, responsiveness, and national reach. A higher referral fee means little if the lender declines deals that a better-fit partner would approve.


Lendflow gives brokers access to a network of 75+ vetted lenders and shows the resulting offers in one view. Lendflow reports that brokers on its platform see 2.4x more competitive offers per deal.


#### Prepare Files That Move Quickly


Lendflow's pre-qualified offers drive an average of 42% faster speed to funding, and Lendflow reports that brokers see 35% less time to close. Speed starts with the file, which means organized financials, a clear borrower résumé, and a solid understanding of any business being acquired.


Answer lender requests quickly, because open items slow underwriting for everyone involved. Lendflow's guide on how to[optimize deal flow to funding](https://www.lendflow.com/post/how-brokers-can-optimize-deal-flow-from-application-to-funding) breaks down where deals stall between application and close.


Manual document handling slows files and adds headcount as volume grows. Lendflow Doc Analyzer provides[automated document data extraction](https://www.lendflow.com/solutions/doc-analyzer) , so brokers spend less time keying data and more time placing deals.


#### Have a Plan for Declines and Harder Deals


Some deals need more work before a lender will approve them. A borrower with declining revenue, or an acquisition buyer with thin industry experience, may need more equity, seller financing, or a different lender.


Decline waterfalls keep those files alive by routing an application to the next lender automatically when one lender passes. Lendflow's[Second Look Marketplace](https://www.lendflow.com/solutions/second-look-marketplace) gives brokers a path to more lenders when a first answer is no.


Business brokers placing SBA acquisition deals can also use Lendflow's[dedicated SBA acquisition workflow](https://www.lendflow.com/post/business-acquisition-sba-loans-for-brokers) , a white-label financing experience. It helps buyers submit acquisition details, upload documents, and review lender offers through one streamlined process.


‍


### Scale Referral Volume Without Growing Overhead


$1.5B+ in offers have been made on the Lendflow platform. Lendflow's embedded finance customers operate with 80% smaller teams while converting similar funding volumes. Brokers can apply the same model by adding lender connections and automated workflows.


SBA referral programs reward brokers who refer qualified, well-prepared deals, follow SBA disclosure rules, and match each borrower to the right lender. Brokers who work across a network of lenders give every file more than one path to funding.


‍


### Frequently Asked Questions About SBA Referral Programs


#### How Do SBA Lender Broker Referral Programs Work?


A broker or advisor refers a qualified small business borrower to an SBA lender, which underwrites, closes, and funds the loan. Any compensation paid to the broker is disclosed on SBA Form 159.


#### How Much Can Brokers Earn From SBA Loan Referrals?


Lendflow reports that brokers commonly earn 1% to 3% of the funded amount, paid by the lender. SBA sets no numeric cap but requires reasonable, disclosed fees, and an agent cannot be paid by both borrower and lender for one service.


#### What Is an SBA Preferred Lender and Why Does It Matter for Brokers?


A Preferred Lender holds SBA delegated authority to process, close, service, and liquidate certain 7(a) loans without prior SBA review. For brokers, that authority can reduce SBA review steps before a decision on a referred borrower.


#### What Is the Difference Between a Bank and a Non-Bank SBA Lender?


Non-bank SBLCs are non-depository lenders that SBA licenses to make 7(a) loans and supervises directly. Their credit policies can differ from those of banks, so the same borrower may get different answers from each.


#### How Long Does It Take to Close an SBA Loan?


Timing depends on the loan type, document readiness, and how quickly third parties deliver required reports. Complete files and fast responses to lender requests help keep a deal moving.
